question: What is the meaning of waste system in relation to service system?
description: The circular economy aims to minimize waste and maximize the reuse and recycling of materials, transforming the built environment to promote sustainable production and consumption. Circular economy components include circular business models, design practices, and reverse logistics, supported by policies, standards, regulations, markets, consumer behavior, culture, and technologies. In Austria, the reuse or recycling of materials embedded in buildings would reduce dependency on imports, as the amount of secondary raw materials is larger than primary resources for many materials. The waste system in relation to the service system refers to the transformation of waste into valuable resources, promoting sustainability and reducing environmental impact.

references.text:
The circular economy is a system that enables resource efficiency by 
minimizing waste and maximizing the reuse and recycling of materials 
(Ellen MacArthur, 2013). It aims to eradicate waste and pollution, and 
support the longevity of products and materials, thereby preserving, 
restoring, and regenerating natural capital (Sch¨oggl et al., 2023). In the 
built environment, where the construction and operation of buildings 
account for a significant portion of global resource consumption and 
waste generation, transformation to the circular economy offers a 
promising solution to promote sustainable production and consumption 
as well as reduce the resulting environmental and societal impact 
(Calzolari et al., 2021). Circular economy, as depicted in Fig. 1, includes 
components such as circular business model (Ranta et al., 2018), circular

et al., 2023) and it is supported by enables of circularity such as policies, 
standards, regulations, markets, consumer behavior, culture and tech­

The European Union (EU) describes secondary raw materials 
as “waste that can be recycled is injected back into the economy as 
secondary raw materials” (Eurpoean Commison, 2021). In the existing 
building stock, a large amount of materials is incorporated, which might 
be valuable materials for reuse or recycling. However, these materials 
mostly lead to waste at the end of their life-cycle. In Austria, the amount 
of secondary raw materials is even larger than the primary resources for 
many materials. Since Austria is a country that strongly depends on 
imports, reuse or recycling of materials embedded in buildings would 
reduce the dependency on imports. In many European countries, the 
situation is similar: due to a low amount of primary resources, an import 
of raw materials is necessary (Brunner and Rechberger, 2016). New 
strategies dealing with the wasteful processes are urgently needed.
